correctness.rationale: The projector decomposition is exact. For \(0<s\le1/2\), the characteristic roots yield a positive decreasing response; for \(s>1/2\), an explicit damped-trigonometric representation yields uniform tail bounds. Exact low-index inequalities prove \(u_k>-1/11\) for all remaining cases, with rationally bounded exponential constants. Matrix nonnegativity is equivalent to \(-1/(m-1)\le u_k\le1\). For \(m\ge13\), \(s=3\) gives \(u_2<-1/12\) by \(e^3>16\). The standalone checker verifies symbolic rational recurrences and supporting inequalities; finite sampling is not used as the infinite proof.

evidence: The 2002 report treats positivity/monotonicity for classes of general linear multistep problems and specifies starting procedures. Its generic restrictions cannot be identified with a uniform complete-graph all-step dimension classification.

The 2010 report gives sharp general coefficient-based bounds/monotonicity conditions. Its scalar test-equation and convolution recurrence machinery is relevant, but the inspected discussion does not give a lower envelope valid under exact exponential start and translate it into the 12/13 vertex cutoff.
A-stability bounds spectral amplification, whereas the claimed positivity lower bound depends on the minimum allowed diagonal of \(J+u(I-J)\) and on m.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem asserting entrywise positivity for every generator in a class containing uniform complete graphs under exact exponential startup and all timesteps would imply this claim; a general impossibility theorem would not provide the sharp smallest dimension. The primary literature compared is broader in method class, but its hypotheses/conclusions do not directly settle the quantified family.

evidence: Hundsdorfer--Ruuth--Spiteri 2002: general multistep monotonicity plus starting procedures. It recognizes nontrivial BDF2 positivity constraints but does not, in inspected sections, bound complete-graph exact-start scalar minima at -1/11.
Hundsdorfer--Mozartova--Spijker 2010: coefficient-based stepsize restrictions for generic methods, not a necessary-and-sufficient threshold in graph dimension.
Hundsdorfer 1998: convection-focused BDF2 blends, not the exact homogeneous diffusion semigroup starting operation.
A generic result about loss of unconditional monotonicity does not force failure at \(m=13\) nor ensure success up to \(m=12\). Conversely the present result is not a general monotonicity theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The proved conclusion demands exact exponential startup, uniform complete-graph generator, all positive stepsizes and all time indices, and \(m\le12\) iff positivity. None of the materially compared theorems is shown to imply every component of that conclusion. The work does not claim the known scalar recurrence and spectral reduction as original.

value.rationale: The number of diffusion states is a natural invariant controlling how far a negative decaying mode may be tolerated while transition entries remain nonnegative. The result proves a complete all-stepsize/all-time classification in the simplest homogeneous nontrivial reversible Markov family, with a sharp dimension obstruction distinguishing A-stability from probabilistic validity. Exact exponential startup rules out a spurious artifact of low-order initialization. The threshold is not an arbitrary slice: it is determined by the scalar lower envelope and the complete-graph stationary diagonal \(1/m\).
